units.¿Todos tus clientes merecen la misma ofe: Do all your customers deserve the same offer?
units.Una cadena de electrónica trataba a todo: An electronics chain treated all its customers the same way: the same offers, the same emails and similar discounts. With 6,000 customers and 26 variables, it needed to find behaviour patterns that would let it personalise its campaigns.
units.Seleccioné 9 variables de comportamiento: I selected 9 behavioural variables related to spend, frequency and channel. The analysis identified 4 customer profiles, from premium to at risk of leaving, and matched a strategy to each one.
units.¿Qué pasa con las ventas cuando ocurre a: What happens to sales when something unexpected happens?
units.Una cadena retail podía prever bastante: A retail chain could forecast normal weeks fairly well, but its predictions failed when promotions, strikes or logistics problems came up. The history explained the past, but not always what was happening around it.
units.Comparé dos modelos sobre 156 semanas: u: I compared two models over 156 weeks: one based only on historical sales and another that added five external variables. I validated them with time-based backtesting and simulated more than ten future scenarios.
units.error frente al modelo basado solo en hi: error compared with the history-only model
units.¿A quién estamos a punto de perder?: Who are we about to lose?
units.Una aerolínea clasificaba a sus pasajero: An airline sorted its passengers into three tiers with rigid rules: Basic, Frequent and Premium. But those rules didn’t always reflect how people actually behaved, so it was hard to know who really needed a loyalty action.
units.Probé tres modelos sobre 21 variables de: I tested three models on 21 variables covering flights, spend and incidents, validated them against a baseline and analysed which variables helped tell the different passenger profiles apart.

units.Modelos predictivos, análisis explorator: Predictive models, exploratory analysis and advanced queries. Python and SQL projects applied to real business problems.
units.Machine Learning, Python y SQL. Modelos: Machine learning, Python and SQL. Models and analysis applied to real problems.
units.Machine Learning, análisis exploratorio: Machine learning, exploratory analysis and advanced queries. Python and SQL applied to real problems where the data needs structure, cleaning and a model that answers specific questions.
units.Modelos predictivos y de clasificación a: Predictive and classification models applied to specific business decisions. Each project starts from a specific question and ends with a metric that measures whether the answer works.
units.¿Cuánto venderemos la próxima semana?: How much will we sell next week?
units.Una cadena retail planifica inventario y: A retail chain plans stock and staffing mainly by looking at what it sold the year before. The problem: ordering too much creates excess stock; ordering too little means running out of product when demand rises.
units.Entrené un modelo de previsión con 208 s: I trained a forecasting model on 208 weeks of sales and validated it on another 52 weeks the model had never seen. The aim was to test how far the history could anticipate future demand.
units.¿Qué hace que un cliente elija un vuelo?: What makes a customer choose a flight?
units.Una aerolínea combina precio, escalas, e: An airline combines price, stopovers, luggage and flexibility, but doesn’t know how much each factor weighs in the customer’s decision. And that weight can change with the type of passenger.
units.Analicé 24 combinaciones de vuelo valora: I analysed 24 flight combinations rated by 1,000 customers. Using conjoint analysis, I broke down 24,000 ratings to measure how much each attribute contributes, both for customers as a whole and for each segment.
units.peso de precio y escalas en la decisión: weight of price and stopovers in the decision
units.Ver más proyectos de Machine Learning en: See more machine learning projects on GitHub
units.Análisis exploratorio con Python, aplica: Exploratory analysis with Python, applied to specific business questions. Each project takes a dataset, cleans it, analyses it and ends with a finding that changes the conversation.
units.Una empresa de servicios con tres depart: A services company with three departments needs to decide where to strengthen its team. The assumption is that the longest-serving employees sell more, but nobody has checked it with data.
units.Diagnóstico de nulos, imputación justifi: Null diagnosis, justified imputation, productivity ratios by department and a correlation matrix to test whether age predicts sales.
units.El servicio de orientación de una univer: A university’s guidance service wants to know which habits best predict exam marks, in order to design a tutoring programme aimed at students at risk.
units.Categorización con pd.cut(), comparación: Categorisation with pd.cut(), group comparison by median and percentiles, and a panel of 6 visualisations: histograms, scatter plots, heatmap and pairplot.
units.Una aseguradora de salud quiere reducir: A health insurer wants to cut costs by identifying patients at high cardiovascular risk early, and to decide whether it’s fair to adjust premiums by risk profile.
units.Conversión de categóricas a numéricas, r: Converting categorical variables to numeric, ranking risk factors by sorted correlation and segmenting patients with a multi-metric groupby.
units.Ver más proyectos Python en GitHub\n: See more Python projects on GitHub
units.Consultas avanzadas, exploración de dato: Advanced queries, data exploration and analysis with T-SQL. Each project is self-contained: it creates its tables, loads realistic data and solves business problems with CTEs, window functions and subqueries.
units.Una red de 50 concesionarios del Grupo V: A network of 50 Volkswagen Group dealerships needs to identify its best salespeople, compare performance across brands and segment dealerships by turnover.
units.CTEs encadenadas, subqueries correlacion: Chained CTEs, correlated subqueries, LAG() for month-on-month change, PERCENTILE_CONT for distribution and RANK() for rankings. Every exercise solved with two approaches.
units.AdventureWorks necesita analizar el comp: AdventureWorks needs to analyse its customers’ buying behaviour, rank products by price and measure year-on-year growth per customer to identify the top 10.
units.ROW_NUMBER, RANK, DENSE_RANK, NTILE, sum: ROW_NUMBER, RANK, DENSE_RANK, NTILE, running totals with ROWS BETWEEN, LAG/LEAD for consecutive rows and CTE + LAG for YoY growth. A final exam in the style of a technical interview.
units.Una tienda de alimentación necesita segm: A grocery shop needs to segment customers, classify products, spot buying patterns and build cross rankings by city, category and supplier.
units.LEFT JOIN para detectar gaps, CASE para: LEFT JOIN to find gaps, CASE for business classifications (VIP/standard, frequent/occasional), CTEs + window functions and advanced combinations: top 3 customers per city, an SQL dashboard.
